transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what finally made me come in is that I'm just really struggling with... well, I keep forgetting basic adult things. Like paying my bills. Which is so frustrating because I know I have the money in my account, I just literally forget. 

And returning interview emails! I just finished my bachelor's degree, and the graduation ceremony was outside, which was a total disaster because it rained and my mom was so mad about her hair being ruined—she spent like two hours on it that morning. But anyway, I'm supposed to be job hunting now. But I keep messing it up because I forget to email people back, or I just flat out don't show up for appointments. I'll leave the house to do errands and just completely not follow through on any of them. Like, I think I spent three hours at Target yesterday just smelling every single candle in the home goods aisle instead of buying the laundry detergent I actually went there for. 

But yeah, I'm just dropping the ball on everything, and it's really starting to cost me real opportunities.
Looking back at your life, do you remember struggling with these types of issues—like forgetfulness or trouble staying on task—when you were a child or in elementary school?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Even way back in elementary school, it was a whole thing. Like, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was really bright, but... oh man, report cards. My dad used to stick them on the fridge with these little ladybug magnets. He got them at this craft fair in Vermont when we went for a fall trip once. It was freezing there, I actually had to buy this super itchy wool sweater that I absolutely hated because I forgot a jacket... wait, what was I saying? 

Right, school. So the teachers would write that I constantly lost my worksheets and I always rushed through all the directions on tests. And I talked out of turn constantly. I just always had something to say, you know? Like if someone mentioned dogs, I had to immediately tell everyone about my neighbor's golden retriever who used to literally eat the mail. The mailman was so mad, he actually threatened to stop delivering to their house. 

But yeah, and my desk... my desk was a complete disaster zone. It was so incredibly messy I could never find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. I actually found a three-week-old turkey sandwich crushed in the back of it once. It was so gross. I don't even eat turkey anymore because of that. Or swiss cheese. Swiss cheese just has a really weird texture anyway, don't you think?
In your daily life as an adult, do you feel like you are often driven by a motor, find it difficult to sit still for long periods, or frequently interrupt others when they are speaking?

Yeah, definitely. It's like I can't just... exist, you know? Even without a job right now, I'm just constantly moving from one thing to the next all day long. Like I'll start the laundry, then I'll remember I need to check my emails, but then I end up just reorganizing all the tabs on my browser. I have this color-coding system for my tabs now, which is actually super cool. Blue is for social media, green is for job stuff, and pink is for random things I want to buy. I actually found this really cute pair of boots on one of the pink tabs yesterday, but they were sold out in my size. Which is the worst, right? Why do they even leave the picture up if they don't have the sizes? 

But anyway, yeah, I'm just always pacing around the apartment or starting dinner at like 3 PM because I feel like I have to be doing *something*. It's like I cannot let myself just stop and sit down, even when I realize that literally none of the things I'm doing are actually getting finished. I just keep going and going. And interrupting people... yeah, my mom gets so mad at me for that. I just get so excited about what I want to say that it just sort of bursts out of me before I can stop it.
